dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Hi, Lorraine. Before anything else, could I get your name again? Lorraine, and the last name?
Lorraine Medeiros, M-E-D-E-I-R-O-S.

Well, that's funny, that's my last name too. Isabel Medeiros. Same spelling. Anyway. I'm writing this down as we go, I like to keep a record. I'm calling about a catch basin at the corner by my house that's clogged with leaves. Every time it rains the water backs right up into my driveway.
Okay, Isabel, I'm going to write that down too. A catch basin clogged with leaves, and water backing up into your driveway. What's the address?
112 Coggeshall Avenue. That's up on the Historic Hill. The drain's at the corner, maybe forty feet from my driveway.
112 Coggeshall Avenue. And when did this happen most recently?

The rain Friday into Saturday, two days ago. It came down all day Friday and into Saturday, and the whole corner turned into a pond. The leaves are packed in that grate from the fall. Nobody has cleaned it. I've looked at it, it's solid leaves, you can't even see the openings.
Right. So the grate is covered over, and the water has nowhere to go but across the street and into your drive.

Exactly. And it's not just me. The cars are slowing to a crawl going through it. People creep through because they don't know how deep it is, and then there's a line backed up behind them. Saturday afternoon I counted six cars waiting at once.
That's a lot for that street. Did any water get into the house or the garage?

No, it stopped at the top of the driveway. But it was close, and I shouldn't have to watch it every time it rains. This is not the first time the water's pooled there. It's been like that since the leaves came down, and every storm it's the same thing.

I understand. Let me make sure I have it right. Corner near 112 Coggeshall, catch basin blocked with leaves, water ponding and running into your driveway, traffic crawling through. Is that the corner closest to you, or is it across the street?
It's on my side, the corner just downhill from my driveway. The grate is on the curb right at the corner.
Okay, on your side, downhill at the corner.
Can I ask something? Is that a city drain or a state one? Because I've heard some of the roads around here belong to the state, and I don't want to be sending this to the wrong place and have it sit.

Good question. Coggeshall is a city street as far as I know, so the drain on it should be ours. If it turns out to be a state structure, we'd pass it along to them ourselves, so you wouldn't have to chase it.
All right. So you'll handle the handoff if there's one.
Yes. I'll note it on the work order so whoever goes out checks that first.

Good. Because honestly, I'm tired of this. I spent part of Saturday out there with a rake trying to pull leaves out of the grate, and it didn't do much. The water was too fast and the grate was packed down.
Please don't stand in the street when it's like that. Traffic and the water both. We'd rather you call us.
Well, I am calling you. That's the point. Let me get this down. What do I write for the work order? Is there a number?
Let me put it in and see what it gives me. [pause] Okay, it's generating now. I'll read it out, and you tell me when you've got each part.
Go ahead, I've got my pen.
It's request number 4, 1, 7, 2.
Four, one, seven, two. Got it.
And it's logged as a clogged catch basin, 112 Coggeshall Avenue, with water backing into a private driveway and slowed traffic.
Okay. Now, when does somebody come? Because I want to write that down too.
The drain crews are working through a list after that rain, and there's a lot of leaf debris everywhere this time of year. I'd say you're looking at a few days, maybe up to the end of the week.
The end of the week. So Friday.
Give or take. If it's the weekend you'd see it Monday at the latest. If it rains again before then, call back and we'll push it up the list.
I'll do that. I have to say, I've got a rainy forecast I've been watching, so I'd really prefer they got there first.
I'll mark it as a repeat problem with traffic impact, which helps move it along.

Thank you. I do like when things are written down properly. I paint miniatures, little figures for a tabletop game, so I'm used to being careful with details. I sit at the table by the front window for hours, and that's how I see that corner all day. I watch the cars splash through.
That must be a good view of the problem, then. It helps to have someone who notices.
Well, I notice, and then nothing happens. Anyway. Do you need a callback number from me?
Yes, please, in case the crew needs to reach you about the driveway. What's a good number?
401-555-0198. That's the landline, and I'm home most of the day.
401-555-0198. Let me read that back. Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-nine-eight.
That's right.

Great. So to recap, I have request 4172, the catch basin at the corner near 112 Coggeshall Avenue, clogged with leaves, a few days to the end of the week for the crew, and a note to check whether it's city or state.
Yes. Four-one-seven-two, end of the week. Thank you, Lorraine. And I'll write your name next to it, Medeiros with the same spelling.
Well, you do that. Call me back if nobody's been by. Have a good afternoon, Isabel.
You too. Goodbye.
